title: Run budget per card
summary: AGT-2955 was killed at the host-wide 90-minute RUNNER_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS four times on 28 and 29 September (fences 3, 6, 7, 8; the card reports five). Salvage kept every file (identical patch-ids in every later chain), but each round started a fresh session on the integration branch, cherry-picked the salvage itself, and lost verification state and in-flight diagnosis: the two operator redeliveries spent 84 of 86 and 84 of 90 minutes rerunning builds and suites at load 27 on 12 cores and added no change. The one AGT-2861 automatic continuation delivered in 29 minutes. Four alternatives compared (raise host timeout, per-card budget only, budget with soft-limit checkpoint and same-session continuation, verification offload). Recommended: a per-card budget (card, project, operator, host, clamped to a host ceiling), a soft limit at 0.8 of the budget that triggers a same-session checkpoint turn, continuation on the salvage in the same session when the continuation ledger admits it, progress-gated automatic rounds, and an operator decision (raise, cut, stop) at the third exhaustion per delivery, shown in a Run budget section on the card. Five implementation slices.

implementationTasks.title: Run-budget ledger per card and delivery
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, docs/system/domains/runner.md, docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html (read before changing run-outcome, retry or continuation logic; append a case-log entry after), and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-2998 run-budget Dossier. Use the Dossier's recommended option for every open decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

## Goal
Give the backend one authoritative record of how much run budget a card has used in its current delivery, so later slices can gate continuations and the card can show it.

## Scope
- Add typed non-terminal outcomes `BudgetCheckpoint` and `BudgetExhausted` next to today's `unknown`/`Timeout` completion. For now, map a remote completion with reported reason `Timeout` to `BudgetExhausted`. RB-S3 emits `BudgetCheckpoint`.
- Derive a per-card budget ledger from `session-continuation-ledger.jsonl` (`SessionContinuationLedgerEntry.DurationSeconds`, tokens, result ref/SHA) plus the completion facts: one entry per round with trigger, start and end, minutes, typed outcome, salvage ref and SHA, start tree SHA, end tree SHA, and `progress` (true when the end tree differs from the start tree, or when a checkpoint records a passing verification on a tree not verified before).
- Count exhaustions per card per delivery. The counter resets only on an accepted delivery or on an operator decision that changes budget or scope (RB-S5 writes that event). An operator requeue, `/continue` without such a decision, or an infrastructure redelivery must not reset it. Note that today `CountAutomaticRounds` resets per review-attempt epoch; keep that method for AGT-2861 compatibility until RB-S4 replaces its use.
- Expose the projection read-only on the task detail API: `runBudget { perRoundMinutes, source, exhaustionsUsed, exhaustionsAllowed, minutesUsed, rounds[], nextStep }`. `source` and `perRoundMinutes` may be the host default until RB-S2 lands.

## Out of scope
Changing timeouts, runner behaviour or the frontend.

## Acceptance criteria
- A replayed AGT-2955-shaped history (fix round timeout, automatic continuation delivered, fix round timeout, two operator requeues with timeouts) projects 4 exhaustions and marks the round whose end SHA equals its start SHA as progress=false.
- An operator requeue and an infrastructure redelivery do not reset the exhaustion counter; an accepted delivery does. Each case has a unit test.
- The task detail API returns the runBudget projection, and the contract is documented in docs/system/domains/runner.md.
- The existing AGT-2861 breaker test (RunTimeoutContinuationBreakerTest) still passes unchanged.

implementationTasks.title: Per-card run budget resolution and transport
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, docs/system/domains/runner.md, docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html (read before changing run-outcome, retry or continuation logic; append a case-log entry after), and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-2998 run-budget Dossier. Use the Dossier's recommended option for every open decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

## Goal
Replace the single host-wide run limit with a budget resolved per card and sent to the runner in the run spec.

## Scope
- Resolution order: operator override on the card (audited, scope `next-round` or `delivery`), then the card field `runBudgetMinutes`, then the project default in application project settings, then the host `RUNNER_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Clamp to a new host ceiling `RUNNER_RUN_BUDGET_MAX_SECONDS` (default 14400). A card value above the project cap (default 150 min) is refused with a clear error unless an operator override sets it.
- Add `RunBudgetSeconds` and `RunBudgetSource` to `RunSpecDto` (additive, an older server omits them) on both the monolith and the standalone Task Server claim paths. The runner passes the budget into `DurableAgentProcess.Start(..., timeoutSeconds: ...)`. The mechanical-resume 300-second ceiling keeps precedence for mechanical rounds.
- The runner logs `[runner] run-budget seconds=<n> source=<card|project|operator|host>` and ships it to the run log.
- Add an operator API to set and clear the override. It records actor and reason on the timeline.
- Document the new variables in docs/operations/setup/linux-runner-host.md and runner.env.template.

## Out of scope
Soft limit, continuation and UI beyond what the API needs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover each resolution source, the project cap refusal, the host ceiling clamp, and an older server that omits the field (the host default applies).
- A runner test proves a card budget of 120 minutes reaches the detached job spec as 7200 seconds, and that a mechanical resume still uses its 300-second ceiling.
- The run log contains the run-budget line with the correct source for a card-level and a host-default run.
- The override API is audited (actor, reason, scope) and covered by an endpoint test.

implementationTasks.title: Soft limit and checkpoint turn in the runner
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, docs/system/domains/runner.md, docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html (read before changing run-outcome, retry or continuation logic; append a case-log entry after), and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-2998 run-budget Dossier. Use the Dossier's recommended option for every open decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

## Goal
End a round with a checkpoint instead of a kill.

## Scope
- At `softLimit = min(0.8 * budget, budget - 600 s)` the runner interrupts the running CLI and resumes the same session (car engine `ResumeSessionId`) with a fixed checkpoint prompt stored under `prompts/runtime/`. The checkpoint turn is capped at 10 minutes and never runs past the hard limit.
- Checkpoint prompt contract: stop starting new work, do not commit, write `results/checkpoint.md` with the headings `Done`, `Verified` (command, result, tree SHA it ran on), `In progress` (open diagnosis, hypotheses, last evidence), `Next step`, and `Remaining steps`, then end with the normal terminal sentinel rules.
- The runner salvages as today and reports outcome `BudgetCheckpoint` when `checkpoint.md` exists, otherwise `BudgetExhausted`.
- Lift the `RUNNER_CLI_RESUME_ARGS` gate only for this checkpoint path on the car engine, behind the parity scenario the RemoteTaskRunner comment defers to T2/T3 (P12). The legacy engine and CLIs without resume fall back to: deadline and checkpoint instructions in the initial prompt (`AGENT_RUN_DEADLINE_UTC` in the environment), hard-limit salvage, and outcome `BudgetExhausted`.
- The initial prompt of every coding round states the budget and the soft-limit time.

## Verification
This changes `prompts/runtime/`, so run the matching live probe (the `@billable` hello-world spec or an equivalent short-budget probe) and record the result, or state why it could not run.

## Acceptance criteria
- A runner test with a 120-second budget shows the interrupt at the soft limit, a same-session resume with the checkpoint prompt, the 10-minute cap reduced to the remaining budget, salvage, and outcome BudgetCheckpoint.
- When resume is unsupported, the round runs to the hard limit, salvages, and reports BudgetExhausted; the initial prompt contains the deadline.
- A live probe or the documented reason for not running it is recorded in results/.
- docs/system/domains/runner.md and the drive-to-conclusion case log describe the checkpoint turn.

implementationTasks.title: Continuation from salvage in the same session
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, docs/system/domains/runner.md, docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html (read before changing run-outcome, retry or continuation logic; append a case-log entry after), and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-2998 run-budget Dossier. Use the Dossier's recommended option for every open decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

## Goal
Make the continuation after a budget checkpoint or exhaustion start where the previous round stopped, in files, session and verification state, and continue automatically only while rounds make progress.

## Scope
- For `BudgetCheckpoint` and `BudgetExhausted`, prepare the next worktree on the salvage commit via `ContinuationBaseStore` (as `RunContinuationCause.WorkerLost` already does), so the agent no longer fetches or cherry-picks the salvage.
- Add a budget-continuation admission beside `MechanicalSessionResumePolicy`: same task, provider, repository, worktree path and clean-context identity; captured session present on the host; total tokens under a ceiling. When admitted, resume the session with a short prompt (`Budget round n of 3 started; your checkpoint is in results/checkpoint.md; continue with Next step`). Otherwise start clean with the original card prompt plus `checkpoint.md` as the handoff, instead of appending another STEER block to prompt.md. Stop pinning `CliContextModes.Clean` for these rounds.
- Replace the fixed `MaxAutomaticContinuationRounds = 1` for budget outcomes with the RB-S1 ledger: automatic continuation while exhaustions < 3 and the previous round had progress=true. Otherwise escalate with the salvage named (RB-S5 turns that escalation into the decision gate). Update the loop-inventory entry `completion.run-timeout-salvage-continuation` and its breaker test to the new bound.
- Continuation prompt rule: rerun only commands whose inputs changed since the verified tree SHA in the checkpoint, plus targeted tests; leave the declared routine suites to the platform gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- Replay test: after a BudgetCheckpoint, the next claim carries ContinuationBaseRef/Sha, the worktree HEAD equals the salvage SHA, and the session is resumed when admitted.
- Admission refusals (provider change, worktree path mismatch, missing session, token ceiling) each start clean with checkpoint.md in the prompt and record the refusal reason in the ledger.
- A round with progress=false escalates instead of continuing; a third exhaustion escalates; the breaker test asserts both bounds.
- prompt.md does not grow by a STEER block for budget continuations.

implementationTasks.title: Run-budget operator decision and card section
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, docs/system/domains/runner.md, docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html (read before changing run-outcome, retry or continuation logic; append a case-log entry after), and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-2998 run-budget Dossier. Use the Dossier's recommended option for every open decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

## Goal
Turn the third exhaustion (or a round without progress) into an explicit operator decision, and show the budget on the card.

## Scope
- On escalation from RB-S4, create a typed gate item `run-budget-decision` on the card in `5e-escalated`, with the RB-S1 projection and a rule-based suggestion: raise when at least 60 % of the last round was build/test command time; cut when the diff grows and the checkpoint lists more than 3 remaining steps; stop and re-plan after two rounds without progress. Show the numbers behind the suggestion.
- Actions: raise the budget (120/150/180/240 min, scope next round or delivery, grants one more round), cut smaller (delivers the verified partial state as the card scope and creates follow-up cards from `Remaining steps` via the Task API; read .agents/skills/task-api/SKILL.md first), and stop (park or archive with the salvage in the reason). Each action writes the operator decision event that RB-S1 uses to reset or extend the allowance.
- `/continue` without one of these actions requires a reason, records `budget-retry-unchanged`, and counts as an exhaustion. Infrastructure or night-shift redelivery automation must skip cards escalated with `run-budget-decision`.
- Frontend: add a `Run budget` section on the card detail next to the run history, following frontend/AGENTS.md, docs/quality/design/style-guide-hard-rules.md and the admin flat-surface guideline. It shows budget and source, exhaustions used of the allowance, minutes used, one row per round (trigger, minutes, typed outcome with dot and label, progress, copyable salvage SHA), and the next step with the three actions. No coloured left accent bars; use central tokens and standard components.

## Acceptance criteria
- Backend tests: the gate item appears at the third exhaustion and after a progress=false round; each action produces the documented lane move, allowance change and timeline entry; redelivery automation skips the card.
- Playwright spec with a deterministic fixture renders the section in light and dark themes; screenshots of both are saved under results/ and show the dot plus label, the suggestion, and the three actions.
- The docs/run-budget-per-card/index.html Implementation log gets an entry for each slice as it lands; the Decision sections stay unchanged.
- docs/system/domains/tasks.md documents the gate item and actions.
